title: The End of the Beginning
coreMove: Audit a successful transition so the hard years become durable judgment rather than a clean victory story.
sourcePressure: The ending separates outcome from interpretation, asks which crisis tactics should stop, which principles travel, and what identity shift remains after success.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is closure as celebration, relief, or lessons learned after victory.

exampleSpecs.domain: family-owned medical imaging center sold to a regional health system
exampleSpecs.audience: a former owner deciding which crisis habits to carry into an integration role
exampleSpecs.stakes: the sale solved capital pressure but left staff distrust from the survival period
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner separates the outcome line from the cost line on the integration plan, then marks which emergency habits must stop before meeting staff
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a signed purchase agreement lying beside a staff retention list

exampleSpecs.domain: software tools company after a successful open-source foundation transfer
exampleSpecs.audience: a project founder no longer controlling every release decision
exampleSpecs.stakes: continuing crisis control could weaken the community the transfer was meant to protect
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the founder writes which release controls were necessary during survival and removes two controls now that foundation governance exists
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a governance charter open beside an old emergency release checklist

exampleSpecs.domain: regional apparel manufacturer emerging from bankruptcy protection
exampleSpecs.audience: a plant owner whose creditors approved the plan but whose supervisors still act like every week is existential
exampleSpecs.stakes: old urgency preserves discipline but may keep breaking normal planning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner lists which bankruptcy tactics saved cash, which now distort planning, and which operating principle deserves to remain
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bankruptcy exit order beside a new production calendar

exampleSpecs.domain: public library system after passing a rescue levy
exampleSpecs.audience: a library director whose advocacy campaign won but left staff exhausted
exampleSpecs.stakes: relief could hide the damage done by months of emergency campaigning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director tells branch managers the levy result, names the exhaustion cost, and asks which emergency communication cadence should end immediately
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a certified election result taped beside a branch staffing chart

exampleSpecs.domain: biotech contract research lab after landing a stabilizing master-service agreement
exampleSpecs.audience: a CEO whose team wants to treat the contract as proof every prior shortcut was wise
exampleSpecs.stakes: the lab may keep unsafe shortcuts because success made them look validated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the CEO draws a line between shortcuts that bought survival and standards that must return before the next audit
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a master-service agreement clipped over a deviation log

exampleSpecs.domain: regional bus manufacturer after winning a large municipal order
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations chief who survived layoffs and now must rebuild normal capacity
exampleSpecs.stakes: the new order looks like proof, but the company still carries skill gaps from the cutbacks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chief walks past empty training bays, refuses to call the order the lesson, and writes the three capabilities that must be rebuilt before production ramps
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an empty training bay beside a newly signed municipal purchase order

skillTargets: distinguish durable principles from temporary tactics
identify success stories that erase cost
choose what to carry forward after a transition

tryThisNowSpec: For one completed hard period, draw three columns: outcome, cost, and principle to carry. Put one item in each without letting the outcome explain the other two.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter
